intel.t: Lower costs and fight a rigged system; he calls his opponent special interest Jon who works for billionaires, utilities and Wall Street.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: Husted says Brown spent 32 years in Congress with little to show for it and wants to shut down power plants; outside ads hit him on transgender issues, the theme that helped beat him in 2024.
Independents: Marist, October 15 to 18, had him ahead 50 to 35 among independent likely voters and 48 to 44 overall.
FactCheck.org said his FirstEnergy ads imply wrongdoing by Husted that no one has charged.
He leads in hard dollars but outside spending against him is about $164 million through October 23.

bottom: Brown is the best funded Senate challenger in this set. VoteLog shows $68,409,200 raised through October 14, 2026, with $57,861,942 from individuals and only $1,055,783 from PACs, https://votelog.org/investigations/ohio-senate-general-money. His campaign reported $28.2 million in the third quarter alone, nearly 200,000 donors and an average gift of $39.63, https://www.sherrodbrown.com/2026/10/15/as-record-spending-from-corporate-special-interests-bail-out-husted-sherrod-brown-raises-over-28-2-million-in-q3/. He is also the most heavily targeted: VoteLog shows $164,312,026 in outside spending against him, against $108,391,198 against Husted.
Interests with money and a live decision:

**Crypto.** Fairshake's affiliate Defend American Jobs reported $11.4 million against Brown in its first filing on September 24, 2026, part of a $30 million pledge, https://cointelegraph.com/news/crypto-industry-spending-ohio-senate-race-sherrod-brown. VoteLog now shows $55,760,700 from that group. Brown chaired Senate Banking and was a leading crypto critic. The decision is crypto market structure law in 2027.
**The SMP network.** WinSenate at $62,524,530, Duty And Country, Lower Costs Now and Defend The Vote carry his outside side. SMP funds three of them.

intel.t: Ohio has more jobs than ever; help Ohioans earn more and keep more, with no tax on tips, overtime and Social Security under his Working Families Tax Credit Act.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: FirstEnergy and HB 6, which Brown and outside groups use to call him special interest Jon; FactCheck.org says the ads imply wrongdoing he was never charged with.
His work ethic and poverty remarks, which Brown attacks.
Marist, October 15 to 18, had him down 44 to 48 among likely voters and 35 to 50 among independents.
Musk put more than $7 million behind him as of October 19, 2026.

bottom: Husted is a former Ohio lieutenant governor who sits on Appropriations, EPW, HELP, Small Business and Aging. His campaign has raised $19,894,786 through October 14, 2026, under a third of Brown's, but outside money benefiting him totals $230,846,544, the most of any subject in this batch, per VoteLog, https://votelog.org/investigations/ohio-senate-general-money.
Interests with money and a live decision:
**Party and Trump world.** SLF at $80,413,044 and No Going Back PAC at $27,770,039 lead his outside side. MAGA Inc. funds No Going Back with $200 million across races.
**Crypto.** Defend American Jobs, Fairshake's affiliate, counts $55,760,700 for him and against Brown, the former Banking chair.

D.t: Sherrod Brown leads by 4.9 in the forecast and wins 86% of simulations. The cushion is about 232,510 votes; a one point swing is about 23,823 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +1.0 and D +10.7. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is D +4.6. Your best recent poll is Cook Political Report/GS Strategy Group and New River Strategies at D +6.0; your worst is Rasmussen Reports (R) at R +0.6. 19 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Cuyahoga, a projected net 254,546 votes; Franklin, a projected net 238,084 votes; Hamilton, a projected net 113,384 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Stark, R +5.9, 3.2% of the vote; Delaware, D +6.5, 2.3% of the vote; Lake, D +2.2, 2.2% of the vote; Mahoning, D +9.8, 2.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Sherrod Brown runs furthest behind in Clermont, Warren, Greene. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 86% of voters, 47 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.29 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 68% of voters, 50 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.38 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 49 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.21 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Sherrod Brown: Immigration voters 21 to 76, Small counties 27 to 70, Voters who can afford daily costs 41 to 56. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$16.2M cash against $8.9M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Activity: 7 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Clermont, a projected net 24,156 votes; Warren, a projected net 23,358 votes; Butler, a projected net 20,255 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Stark, R +5.9, 3.2% of the vote; Delaware, D +6.5, 2.3% of the vote; Lake, D +2.2, 2.2% of the vote; Mahoning, D +9.8, 2.0% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jon Husted runs furthest behind in Cuyahoga, Summit, Mahoning. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 86% of voters, 50 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.29 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 68% of voters, 47 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.38 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 48 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.21 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Jon Husted: Black voters 15 to 83, Independents 24 to 70, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 26 to 71. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$8.9M cash against $16.2M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

media.what: His Silver Bulletin forecast gave Sherrod Brown a 73.9% chance to unseat Jon Husted.
Interviewed Ohio Senate candidate Sherrod Brown; the episode page listed it as 5 days old on Oct 22.
Spoke at Trump's Youngstown rally and urged Ohioans to vote Nov 3 so Republicans keep control, without naming candidates.
In a YouTube forecast video listed Ohio as a Democratic lead of 3 points.
Named Ohio among six toss up Senate races and warned Democrats of a big siren because polls are within the margin of error.
Anchored The 11th Hour live from Columbus covering the Ohio Senate contest.
Said he is worried for Republicans in Ohio.
On the Journal Editorial Report called Sherrod Brown a terrific candidate and predicted a horserace with Jon Husted.
Said Sherrod Brown should win, though he could be painted as establishment.
Hosted the Journal Editorial Report segment where Karl Rove weighed the Brown vs Husted and Iowa Senate races.
On Anderson Cooper 360 he said Sherrod Brown holds a four point lead over Jon Husted in Ohio.
Predicted in Reason that Republicans will likely lose the Ohio Senate seat.
